about: The `annual_report_catalogue` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2013 only.

provenance.warning: These figures cite a document not present in the document table, so no address can be given for them. Treat any figure resting on them as uncheckable.

rows.name: Table of contents / department index with page numbers
rows.printed_heading: Balance Sheet / Bonded Indebtedness / Building Inspector / Zoning Official / Capital Planning Committee / ... / Zoning Board of Appeals
rows.what_it_is: Alphabetical index of report sections with the printed page number or range for each.
rows.layout: two columns
rows.notes: Two page ranges print with a full stop instead of a dash ('3.5', '89.93') — read as 3-5 and 89-93. Printed page numbers run 4 lower than the PDF page index.

rows.name: Town at a glance: population, valuation, tax rate and legislative delegation
rows.printed_heading: POPULATION: / DENSITY: / ASSESSED VALUATION: / TAX RATE: / UNITED STATES SENATORS IN CONGRESS: / REPRESENTATIVE IN CONGRESS: / STATE SENATOR: / REPRESENTATIVE IN GENERAL COURT:
rows.what_it_is: Label/value fact block at the head of the report.
rows.layout: two-column label/value list; the ROADS lines are cut off at the top of the page
rows.notes: THIS BLOCK IS A VERBATIM REPRINT OF THE FY2012 ONE and is stale: it gives the 2012 town census (9982), the FY2012 assessed valuation ($1,101,654,500 real estate, $29,375,244 personal property) and 'TAX RATE: $ 17.30 (Fiscal 2013)', while the assessors' own table on p10 gives FY2013 valuation as $1,131,029,744. It also still lists Scott P. Brown as senator and John W. Olver as representative, both of whom had left office. Do not take any figure from this page.

rows.name: Town department office hours
rows.printed_heading: OFFICE HOURS
rows.what_it_is: Opening hours for each town office by day group.
rows.layout: three columns
rows.notes: Identical to FY2012's, including the footer '(TOWN HALL, RITTER MEMORIAL BUILDING AND LUNENBURG PUBLIC LIBRARY AND EAGLE HOUSE CLOSED FRIDAY)' — the four-day week continued.

rows.name: Board and committee regular meeting schedule
rows.what_it_is: When and where each board meets.
rows.grain: one board and one recurring meeting slot
rows.layout: four columns
rows.notes: Differs from FY2012 in ways worth noting: an Assessors row appears, the Historical Commission moves from the Library to Ritter, PACC moves to Eagle House, the Sewer Commission and Cemetery Commission move to the DPW Office, the Zoning Board moves to Town Hall, and the Housing Partnership row disappears. The meeting-location changes track the building consolidation discussed in the Town Manager's report.

rows.name: Elected officials with term-expiry year
rows.printed_heading: BOARD OF HEALTH / BOARD OF ASSESSORS / TRUST FUND COMMISSIONERS / CEMETERY COMMISSIONERS / LIBRARY TRUSTEES
rows.what_it_is: Every elected board with its members and term expiry years.
rows.layout: two column stacks, with a THIRD partially-cropped column of appointed offices bleeding in from the facing page down the right margin
rows.notes: Worse than FY2012's version of the same table. Many year/name pairs are split across two lines ('2013' on one line, the name on the next), and the right-hand margin carries truncated fragments from p7 ('AsS', '201', 'CO!', 'CAP', 'Jam', 'Stev') that must be stripped. The content matches FY2012's board membership closely, so FY2012 is the better source for the overlapping year.

rows.name: Appointed officials, boards and one-year appointments
rows.printed_heading: LOCAL CENSUS LIASON (and the appointed-office headings)
rows.what_it_is: Every appointed position and committee with appointee and expiry year, including the full police roster of patrol and reserve officers.
rows.layout: two to three side-by-side column stacks
rows.notes: p7 is 60 lines and p8 52. Same structure as FY2012 but with more line-splitting between the year and the name.

rows.name: Valuation and Tax History, FY2005-FY2013
rows.printed_heading: Valuation and Tax History / Fiscal Year | Tax Rate | Total Valuation | Accounts | Tax Levy | Change(%)
rows.what_it_is: Nine years of tax rate, valuation, account count, levy and year-on-year levy change.
rows.columns: Fiscal Year | Tax Rate | Total Valuation | Accounts | Tax Levy | Change(%)
rows.layout: six-column table, newest first
rows.notes: FY2013: rate 17.30, valuation 1,131,029,744, 5,054 accounts, levy 19,566,814.57, +3.7154%. Every overlapping year matches the FY2011 and FY2012 reports exactly. Note the account count DROPS from 5,351 to 5,054 while valuation rises — a change in what is being counted, not 297 properties disappearing.

rows.name: Fiscal Year 2013 Abstract of Assessments
rows.printed_heading: Fiscal Year 2013 Abstract of Assessments / Property Class Code/Description | Accts | Class Valuation | Avg.Value
rows.what_it_is: Assessed valuation by DOR property class code, with account counts and average value.
rows.columns: Property Class Code/Description | Accts | Class Valuation | Avg.Value
rows.layout: four-column table
rows.notes: THE BEST OF THE THREE YEARS: every account count is present (unlike FY2011 and FY2012 where most were lost), and the TOTALS row prints BOTH the account total and the valuation total, so both columns check themselves. 3,433 single family homes, 434 condominiums, 578 vacant land parcels, 133 commercial, 30 industrial, 179 personal property accounts, 89 in Chapter 61/61A/61B. The 5,054 also ties to the Accounts column of the valuation history table above. This is the year to take a property-class breakdown from.

rows.name: Assessor's account for exemptions, abatements and overlay, five years
rows.printed_heading: Assessor's Account for Exemptions and Abatements / Description | FY2013 | FY2012 | FY2011 | FY2010 | FY2009
rows.what_it_is: Overlay raised, deficits, charges, potential liability and amount released, FY2009-FY2013.
rows.grain: one overlay line item across five years
rows.columns: Description | FY2013 | FY2012 | FY2011 | FY2010 | FY2009
rows.layout: six-column table
rows.notes: The FY2012 and FY2011 columns agree with the FY2012 report, so the restatement noted between FY2011 and FY2012 settled. The row label 'Charges to 6/30/2010' is still printed in the FY2013 report — the date has never been updated across all three years and does not mean what it says.

rows.name: New growth revenue by fiscal year, FY2005-FY2012
rows.printed_heading: New Growth Revenue / Fiscal Year | Added Valuation | Tax Rate | New Revenues | Change(%)
rows.what_it_is: Valuation added by new construction, the rate applied, revenue produced and change on the prior year.
rows.columns: Fiscal Year | Added Valuation | Tax Rate | New Revenues | Change(%)
rows.layout: five-column table
rows.notes: Adds the FY2012 row the FY2012 report omitted: added valuation 19,124,255 at 16.83, new revenues 321,862, +70.54%. Still one year behind the report's own fiscal year — there is no FY2013 row. Unlike the FY2011 and FY2012 versions, the tax rate column here matches the same year's rate in the valuation history (16.83 for FY2012), so the offset noted in the earlier years does not apply.

rows.name: Persons buried this year, by month
rows.printed_heading: The following is a list of persons who were buried this year. / NAME | AGE | CEMETERY / JANUARY / FEBRUARY / MARCH / APRIL / MAY / JUNE / JULY / AUGUST / SEPTEMBER / OCTOBER / NOVEMBER / DECEMBER
rows.what_it_is: Every burial in the town cemeteries during 2013 with age and cemetery, grouped by month. War service appended to some names.
rows.layout: two side-by-side three-column month stacks, reading normally
rows.notes: THE ROTATION IS FIXED HERE — this table reads the right way up with its column header row at the top, where the FY2012 version is upside down and the FY2011 version has no CEMETERY header at all. Names, ages and N/S cemetery codes are on the same lines. '*Denotes Cremation'. FEBRUARY and OCTOBER have no entries. A few cemetery codes are OCR noise ('ZOnz', 'zz'). Compare with the p92 vitals report, which gives 84 deaths against roughly 40 burials.

rows.name: Capital plan items presented at the 2013 Annual Town Meeting, with the Town Manager's additional recommendations
rows.printed_heading: CAPITAL PLANNING / At the Annual Town Meeting May 2013, the following items, totaling $ 523,483, were presented in the FY14 Plan. / DEPARTMENT   AMOUNT   ITEM / Additional recommendations from the Town Manager, totaling $ 129,000:
rows.what_it_is: The FY14 capital plan as two lists: the Capital Planning Committee's eleven items totalling $523,483 and the Town Manager's four additional items totalling $129,000.
rows.layout: three columns; the header prints AMOUNT before ITEM, and unlike FY2012 the data matches its own header
rows.printed_total: totaling $ 523,483 (main plan) and totaling $ 129,000 (Town Manager's additions)
rows.notes: FOUR SCHOOL DEPARTMENT ROWS HAVE AN AMOUNT AND NO ITEM ($41,400, $55,000, $16,000, $15,000), as do Technology ($45,000) and both Fire Department rows ($215,000 and $37,000) — the ITEM column is empty for seven of the eleven rows, so the largest item in the plan ($215,000, Fire) cannot be identified from this page. Article 14 on p86 gives the funding: $502,687 raised and appropriated plus four named prior-article transfers, $9,925 from Real Estate Receipts Reserved and a $3,000 grant from the Montachusett Historical Society, totalling $523,483; plus $129,000 from Free Cash for the Town Manager's additions, i.e. $652,483 in all.

rows.name: Library statistics for 2013
rows.what_it_is: Library operating statistics as a bulleted list, following a note on state certification.
rows.layout: bulleted list split across the p13/p14 page break
rows.notes: MOSTLY LOST. Only one bullet survives on p14 ('Total number of programs provided by the LPL was 167, covering all age groups') and the rest of the list is missing at the page break; the narrative separately gives $11,709 in State Aid Funding for meeting the State Board of Library Commissioners' standards. FY2012's equivalent list is complete and should be used as the model for what is missing here.

rows.layout: label with dot leaders, count right
rows.notes: THE MOST COMPLETE OF THE THREE YEARS: Lunenburg Office (days) 86, Food Service 35, Beach/Camp 30, Housing & Nuisance 26, Septic Test Applications 57, Septic Plan Applications 45, Septic Plan Reviews 48, Septic Permits new lots 24, upgrades 21, Construction Inspections 75. Only 'Septic System Lot Tests' loses its count. The narrative separately reports 73 Title 5 private septic inspections reviewed (up from 51 in FY2012). Note the Lunenburg Office days figure jumps from 18 in FY2012 to 86 here, which is a different quantity or a different counting rule, not a fivefold increase in service.

rows.name: Nashoba Nursing Service & Hospice visit and clinic counts
rows.printed_heading: Nashoba Nursing Service & Hospice / Home Health / Home Health Aide Visits ..... / Rehabilitative Therapy Visit / Medical Social Service Visits... / Hospice Volunteer and Spiritual Care Visits... / Clinics / Local Well Adult, Support Groups, & Other Clinic Visits......

rows.layout: label with dot leaders, count right
rows.notes: Rehabilitative Therapy 455, Medical Social Service 31, Hospice Volunteer/Spiritual 7, Clinic Visits 383, Flu Clinics 171, Well Adult Clinics 143. THE NURSING VISITS LINE IS MISSING ENTIRELY — its label has been absorbed into the explanatory paragraph, so the headline figure (1136 in FY2011, 1177 in FY2012) has no FY2013 value here. rows.name: Roster of the Lunenburg Fire Department

rows.printed_heading: Administrative / Reserve Intermittent Officers

rows.notes: The top of p27 is a badge/patch graphic whose text OCR'd as rubble ('(POLICE LUNENBURG', 'PATBOLMAN', 'EUTENAWT SERGEANT') and must be discarded — it is not roster content. The Sir Robert Peel quotation and the mission statement are prose.

rows.name: Police activity charts: calls for service, arrests and incidents, 2009-2013
rows.printed_heading: INCIDENTS, ARRESTS, CALL FOR SERVICE / Calls For Service / ARRESTS / INCIDENTS
rows.what_it_is: Three bar charts of police workload over five years, with a legend by year.
rows.layout: charts with axis scales and year legends, no data labels
rows.notes: NO DATA VALUES AT ALL — only the axis scales (0-16000 for calls, 0-600 for arrests) and the 2009-2013 legends survived. The narrative carries what is usable and it is unusually specific: calls for service up approx. 6.8% a year over five years and 12.2% this year, implying about 1,000 more calls next year; arrests up 10.4% a year, implying 59 more; incidents up 8.7% since 2009, implying 83 more; burglary/house breaks up 35%, larceny from a motor vehicle up 83%, larceny up 17%; and a workload analysis finding that 630 hours of patrol-only functions could not be performed by 11 patrolmen during the year. Also here: single family residences risen to 3,443 since 2008 and condominium units up 246, which cross-checks the p10 abstract's 3,433 single family accounts.

rows.name: District enrollment by grade, school and residency category, October 2013
rows.what_it_is: Head count by grade, split by resident / school choice / non-resident (Shirley agreement), with a subtotal per school building.
rows.layout: five-column table with Primary Total, THMS Total and LHS Total subtotal rows
rows.notes: RICHER THAN FY2012's ENROLLMENT TABLE — it breaks each grade by residency status and subtotals by building, which FY2012's does not. But the COLUMN HEADER ROW AND THE FIRST FOUR GRADE ROWS (PK through 3) ARE MISSING at the top of the page, so the column meanings must be inferred from the narrative on p32 (1,551 resident, 44 school choice, 7 non-resident Shirley, 1,602 total) and the Primary Total row (517 + 4 + 0 = 521). Several cells are blank where the value is presumably zero. The narrative also gives 292 students with disabilities (18.4%), 22 receiving services outside the district, 17 day and 5 residential placements — placement counts again published here.

rows.name: Special education CPI ratings by grade and subject, Lunenburg against state
rows.printed_heading: Indicator 3C - Proficiency Rate for Students with IEPs on MCAS. For the 2012 MCAS, Lunenburg Students with Disabilities CPI ratings were as follows: / Grade | Subject | Lunenburg | State
rows.what_it_is: Composite Performance Index for students with IEPs, by grade and subject, against the state figure.
rows.layout: four-column table
rows.notes: Grades 3 to 8 across Reading/ELA, Mathematics and Science. Lunenburg beats the state in every row shown. The table runs to the bottom of p34 and its last rows (grade 8 Mathematics and any grade 10 rows) are cut at the page break. Note the subject naming changes mid-table — 'Reading' for grades 3-4, 'ELA' for grades 5-8 — which will break a naive join.

rows.name: Special education DESE indicator results, Lunenburg against state
rows.printed_heading: SPECIAL SERVICES DEPARTMENT / FY13 (data taken from 2012-2013 school year) / Julianna Bahosh, Director of Special Services / Indicator 1 - Graduation Rate. / Indicator 5 - Educational Environments for Students Aged 6-21 with IEPs. / Indicator 6 - Educational Environments for Students Aged 3-5 with IEPs. / Indicator 9 & 10 ... Disproportionality ... / Indicator 11 - Initial Evaluation Timelines. / Indicator 13- Secondary Transition.
rows.what_it_is: Each DESE special education indicator with Lunenburg's rate, the state's rate and, where applicable, the state target.
rows.grain: one indicator (and, within indicators 5 and 6, one placement category)
rows.layout: prose paragraphs, one per indicator
rows.notes: Written as prose but every figure is present and paired with its comparator. Indicator 1 graduation rate: Lunenburg 78.6% against a 77.5% target and a 68.6% state rate. Indicator 5 placement mix: Lunenburg full inclusion 77% / partial 8.2% / substantially separate 10.4% / separate-residential 4.5%, against state 58.1 / 19.9 / 15.0 / 6.8 — Lunenburg includes far more and separates far less than the state. Indicator 6 (ages 3-5): Lunenburg 60 / 24 / 8.0 / 8.0 against state 23.9 / 53.4 / 14.0 / 8.7. Indicators 11 and 13 both 100% compliant. Also here: the district's Accountability and Assistance Level is 2, Students with Disabilities are 'Meets Requirements-At Risk (MRAR)', and their cumulative CPI is 50 against a target of 75. Note the p34 narrative gives total enrollment as 1,587 where p32 and p33 give 1,602 — the two special services paragraphs are otherwise identical and one has a stale denominator.

rows.name: Lunenburg Primary School grade 3 MCAS performance distribution
rows.printed_heading: Grade 3 ELA | Advanced | Proficient | Needs Improvement | Warning / Number of Students / Percent of Students / Grade 3 Math | Advanced | Proficient | Needs Improvement | Warning
rows.what_it_is: Spring 2013 grade 3 MCAS results as counts and percentages across the four performance bands, for ELA and Math.
rows.grain: one performance band in one subject
rows.layout: two stacked four-column tables, each with a Number row and a Percent row
rows.notes: ELA counts 20 / 60 / 38 / 2 but the percent row prints only three values (65% spanning Advanced+Proficient, 31%, 2%) — the percent row does not align with the count row. Math is complete on both rows: counts 45 / 52 / 5 / 6, percents 37 / 43 / 13 / 5. The counts and percents do not reconcile for Math either (45 of 108 is 42%, not 37%), so the two rows should be treated as separate assertions. The narrative gives the prior year for comparison: 85% advanced/proficient in Math, of which 27% advanced and 47% proficient.

rows.name: Monty Tech financial report and grants
rows.printed_heading: Financial Report / Grants and Contracts
rows.what_it_is: The district's Educational Plan total and grant income split into state/federal and private/competitive.
rows.layout: prose
rows.notes: FY2012-2013 Educational Plan $24,333,209, a 7.0% increase — a much bigger jump than FY2012's 2.4%, and the report notes spending was held to the Chapter 70 minimum. State and federal grants FELL to $922,132 from $1,407,959, while private and competitive grants ROSE to $358,245 from $20,918, largely on a $248,275 Massachusetts Life Sciences Center award and a $100,000 award from the Executive Office for Administration and Finance. The two streams sum to $1,280,377 and tie to the printed total. This is a clean example of one funding source substituting for another with the operating total barely moving.

rows.name: Salary Administration Plan step definitions (Article 27)
rows.printed_heading: "Step 1 Defined as the first fiscal year of employment (0 - 12 months) / Step 2 Defined as occurring on the successful completion of year 1 of employment / ... / Step 8 Defined as occurring on the successful completion of year 12 of employment"
rows.what_it_is: The eight steps of the town salary schedule, each defined by years of service — the text being struck out, quoted verbatim in the article, together with the language replacing it.
rows.layout: eight quoted lines
rows.notes: NEW. The old schedule advanced at years 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 — an irregular ladder. The replacement language voted unanimously: 'For the first three (3) steps ... advancement shall occur on an annual basis on the employee's employment anniversary date. Upon reaching Step 3, advancement to subsequent steps shall occur every two (2) years thereafter. Step increases shall be subject to Town Manager approval and the availability of sufficient funds.' The Finance Committee reported no additional financial impact. This is the mechanism behind step costs in the payroll, and the dollar values of the steps are not printed anywhere in the report.
